title: The US-China AI Safety Debate
text:
The US-China AI Safety Debate

Laila Khawaja

Gavekal Technologies: Chips | 17 Sep 2026

Dario Amodei’s call to pace frontier AI development has sharpened a US divide between safety advocates and accelerationists. The innate prisoner’s dilemma among leading labs makes coordinated slowdown unlikely. China recognizes many of the same risks but rejects US-led standard setting and the use of safety to justify technology containment aimed at China. China also favors risk management through regulations and state intervention over slowdown. Given these divisions and the broader US-China rivalry, bilateral talks are unlikely to produce binding agreements. Continued dialogue, crisis-communication channels, and narrow cooperation are the most plausible outcomes.
